I1.quote: Using an adsorption setup designed for investigating gas adsorption at high pressures by the volumetric method, isotherms of hydrogen adsorption were measured for FAS-1-05 microporous carbon adsorbent
I1.location: main, pp. 374-375, Results and Discussion (Fig. 1 and Fig. 3; Table 2 'experiment, 0.101 MPa, 77 K')

I2.quote: Microporous FAS-1-05 and FAS-2-05 carbon adsorbents synthesized under laboratory conditions from a furaldehyde-based polymer by thermochemical synthesis were used in the experiments.

I3.quote: As is seen from Fig. 3, at 77 K and 5 MPa, the adsorption reaches a value of 31 mmol/g, i.e., 6.2 wt %.
I3.location: main, p. 375, Results and Discussion, Fig. 3

I4.quote: Searched the full text for a surface area (BET, Langmuir, m2/g, supplier value) and found none. Table 1 gives only micropore volumes, characteristic energies and half-widths from benzene adsorption (TVFM).

I5.quote: Hydrogen adsorption on two samples of active carbon (FAS) produced from furaldehyde by the thermochemical synthesis method is investigated.

notes: English translation of a Russian original (Colloid Journal 2008, 70(3)). Measured H2 uptake: 77 K isotherms to 100 kPa on FAS-1-05 and FAS-2-05 (Fig. 1, Table 2 'experiment' row, 0.101 MPa, 77 K), and FAS-1-05 volumetric isotherms at 77 K (to 5.1 MPa) and 293 K (to 16.1 MPa) in Fig. 3. Most other H2 values (Tables 2 and 3, 20.38 K, 196 K, 300 K, 7 and 20 MPa) are calculated by TVFM and do not count toward I1. The Fig. 3 x-axis is printed 'P, kPa' but the text and caption context give MPa (5.1 and 16.1 MPa), so I3 is recoverable from the text. No retraction, review, thesis or duplicate-data statement found. First applicable code after I1-I3 met and none of not_primary or retracted applying is no_surface_area (I4).
